title: Per-row HTMX lookup endpoint and live matrix updates
description:
Each row in the matrix view fires its own catalog lookup on load (browser-driven parallel fan-out — no background workers needed). Each completion swaps the row in place with its result.

## Endpoint

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/lookup/`:
  - `@login_required`, ownership/staff check.
  - 409 if row.search_status not in `(pending, multiple)` (idempotent re-trigger only on pending/multiple).
  - Set `search_status=searching`, save.
  - Call `find_series_volume(series_title, author, row.volume_number)` (sibling bead bd-zx8).
  - Apply result:
    - 0 candidates → `search_status=no_match`.
    - 1 candidate → `search_status=found`, `candidate_records=[c]`, `selected_candidate_index=0`.
    - 2+ candidates → `search_status=multiple`, `candidate_records=cs`, `selected_candidate_index=0` (default to first; user can change).
  - Save and render the updated row partial.

## Matrix template

- `_series_claim_matrix.html` — wraps the table in a polling-friendly container.
- `_series_claim_row.html` — renders one row with status badge + candidate summary + per-row action buttons (skip / mark-held / pick-different placeholders rendered, behavior in next bead).

## Visual states per row

- `pending` — gray spinner, "queued"
- `searching` — blue spinner, "looking up..."
- `found` — green badge, candidate title + volume + source catalog
- `no_match` — yellow badge, "no match — saved as gap"
- `multiple` — yellow badge, candidate dropdown to pick

## Tests

- Unit: pending → searching → found transitions persist correctly.
- Unit: 409 on subsequent calls when not pending/multiple.
- Unit: cascade exception logs and leaves row in `searching` (or transitions to `no_match` — pick one in implementation; document choice).
- Auth: non-owner non-staff cannot trigger lookup.

## Dependencies

- bd-zx8 (per-volume lookup helper).
- bd-2t3 (model).
- bd-520 (form/create-claim endpoint, which renders the matrix).

Bead: bd-zwg (parent epic)

title: Consider gitignoring generated tailwind.css
description:
`static/css/tailwind.css` is a generated file committed to the repository. CI now exists, so the blocker this ticket was waiting on is gone.

This has already caused one user-visible bug. `ingest/templates/ingest/_notice.html` was added after the last stylesheet build, so `bg-amber-50` and `border-amber-300` were never compiled and the notice rendered with no background and no border. Nothing catches that: the template is valid, the tests pass, and the missing classes are invisible until someone looks at the page.

The failure mode is structural, not a one-off. A generated artifact under version control goes stale whenever a template adds a class and nobody rebuilds, and two branches that both rebuild produce a conflict in a file no one can meaningfully merge by hand.

## Shape

Gitignore the stylesheet and build it in CI and at deploy time. `just tailwind` already exists as the build step, and `catalog/templatetags/static_version.py` stamps the URL from the file's mtime, so a rebuilt file still busts caches.

Check what breaks first: the e2e suite renders real pages, so it needs the stylesheet present before Playwright runs, and the deploy path needs the same step.

## Second problem, same file

Tailwind is scanning `.beads/issues.jsonl`. `static/src/input.css` names four template directories with `@source`, but the scan still reaches the tracker export, so prose in bead descriptions leaks class candidates into the build. Constrain the sources so the stylesheet is derived from templates alone.

    STATUS_CHOICES = [("pending", "Pending"), ("committed", "Committed"), ("cancelled", "Cancelled")]

    series = models.ForeignKey(Series, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)

class SeriesClaimRow(models.Model):
    SEARCH_STATUS_CHOICES = [
        ("pending", "Pending"),
        ("searching", "Searching"),
        ("found", "Found"),
        ("no_match", "No match"),
        ("multiple", "Multiple matches"),
        ("manual_skip", "Skip"),
        ("manual_held", "Mark held"),
    ]

    claim = models.ForeignKey(SeriesClaim, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="rows")
    volume_number = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    search_status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=SEARCH_STATUS_CHOICES, default="pending")
    candidate_records = models.JSONField(default=list, blank=True)

title: Capture volume evidence for multi-volume set records
description:
A photographed volume of a multi-volume set matches a catalog record for the whole set, and every trace of which volume it is gets dropped during parsing.

The Sapirstein Rashi record (LCCN 2001531851) identifies the volume in three fields, none of which the parser reads:

```
505 1  $a --   -- v. 3. Sefer Ṿa-yikṛa = Vayikra = Leviticus.
020    $a 9780899060286 $q (v. 3)
300    $a v. <3   > ; $c 26 cm.
440  4 $a The ArtScroll series
500    $a Sapirstein edition
```

`245` has no `$n` and no `$p` in this record, so reading the part subfields is not enough on its own: for an open-ended set held as one bibliographic record, the volume enumeration lives in the contents note, the ISBN qualifier, and the extent statement.

Capture the formatted contents note, the ISBN qualifier, and the extent statement, and show them on the record page. The volume identity is also known at ingest time — OCR read ויקרא off the title page — and is discarded at confirm, so the ingest side of this belongs with the series and volume work.

title: Record author roles and the statement of responsibility
description:
Author roles are not recorded anywhere. The record-to-author link (`Record.authors` through table) holds only the record and author ids, and `parse_record` reads `245` subfields `$a` and `$b` only, so the statement of responsibility in `$c` is discarded.

For the Sapirstein Rashi volume (LCCN 2001531851), the roles exist in exactly one place in the LC record:

```
245 10 $a [Perush Rashi ʻal ha-Torah] = $b Rashi : the Torah : with Rashi's commentary / $c translated, annotated, and elucidated by Yisrael Isser Zvi Herczeg ; in collaboration with Yaakov Petroff and Yoseph Kamenetsky ; contributing editor, Avie Gold.
700 1  $a Herczeg, Yisrael Isser Zvi.
700 1  $a Petroff, Yaakov.
700 1  $a Kamenetzky, Yosef.
700 1  $a Gold, Avie.
```

The `700` fields carry no `$e` relator term and no `$4` relator code, so no parser can derive the roles from them — the four contributors arrive flat and indistinguishable, and the catalog page lists them alongside Rashi as if all five stood in the same relation to the book.

Two pieces of work, either useful alone:

Transcribe `245$c` into a statement-of-responsibility field on `Record` and show it under the title. This is what the field is for, it needs no interpretation, and it answers "who did what" for a reader.

Add a role column to the record-author link and populate it from `700$e` / `$4` where a catalog supplies them, with the relator code list mapped to display terms. NLI records carry relators more often than this LC record does. Parsing roles out of `$c` prose is not part of this — the transcribed field covers that case.

## Changes

- `ingest/views.py::title_page_upload` (modify):
  - Save uploaded image bytes to `ScanResult.image` (Django ImageField; existing `staging/%Y/%m/%d/` upload_to).
  - Status `awaiting_ocr`, `ocr_output=None`, `candidate_records=[]`.

  - 409 if `scan.status != "awaiting_ocr"`.
  - Read image bytes via `scan.image.read()`; call `extract_metadata_from_image`.
  - On success: set `scan.status = "pending"`, `scan.ocr_output = metadata`, save. Render existing `_ocr_results.html` (which already supports the metadata edit + cascade-search step).
  - On `extract_metadata_from_image` returning None: leave `awaiting_ocr`; return error partial inline (with retry-and-discard affordances).

## Tests

- Upload phase: creates `ScanResult` with image saved, status `awaiting_ocr`, no OCR called (mock at the import boundary, since `pytest-socket` blocks live HTTP).
- `run_ocr` happy path: state transitions correctly, ocr_output populated, partial rendered.
- `run_ocr` 409 on already-processed.
- `run_ocr` OCR-None: state unchanged, error partial rendered.
- Auth check on both endpoints.

description:
Add real-time barcode scanning via the phone/laptop camera to the ISBN scan page (ingest/templates/ingest/isbn_scan.html).

Current state: The page has a manual ISBN text input that POSTs to the isbn_lookup HTMX endpoint. The camera viewfinder area shows a placeholder message.

1. Add a JavaScript barcode library. Two options:
   - Barcode Detection API (navigator.ml.barcodeDetector): native in Chrome and Safari on mobile, zero dependencies, but not available in Firefox. Check for support and fall back gracefully.
   - QuaggaJS (or its maintained fork @nicolo-ribaudo/quagga2): works everywhere, heavier (~100KB). Use as fallback when Barcode Detection API is unavailable.

7. The JS can be inline in the template or in a separate static file (static/js/barcode-scan.js). Keep it simple — no build step.

title: Normalize publisher strings before catalog search queries
description:
The publisher string extracted by OCR goes into the CQL query verbatim, and exact-phrase matching against the catalog's publisher index is sensitive to corporate suffixes and punctuation. A title page reading "Mesorah Publications, Ltd." produces a query that matches nothing, so the `title+publisher` step returns empty and `run_cascade` falls through to the broad title-only step. The publisher is effectively ignored and the candidate list is dominated by unrelated editions.

Measured against NLI SRU with the same title:

```
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications, Ltd."   0 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications"         2 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah"                      2 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="ArtScroll"                    1 hit
```

Add a normalization helper in `sources/cascade.py` that strips trailing corporate suffixes (Ltd, Ltd., Inc., LLC, GmbH) and trailing punctuation before a publisher value is formatted into a CQL template, and apply it in the cascade steps that use `{publisher}`. Unit tests should cover the suffix forms, a publisher that needs no change, and confirmation that an empty result after normalization still falls through rather than erroring.

Consider whether a `publisher+keywords` step belongs in the cascade for multi-volume works, where the volume title on the title page is not the catalog title: the Sapirstein edition volume photographed as ויקרא is cataloged as "Rashi : the Torah : with Rashi's commentary", so no title-constrained query can reach it, while `alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications" AND alma.all_for_ui="Rashi"` returns it.

title: Volume number normalization helper for series matching
description:
Provide a helper that maps a volume designation (as it appears in MARC 490\$v / 830\$v / 245\$n) to a canonical form for cross-record comparison. Needed so the per-volume catalog lookup can match results back to user-specified volume numbers.

## Surface forms to handle

- Arabic digits: "3", "v. 3", "vol. 3", "volume 3", "pt. 3", "no. 3"
- Roman numerals: "iii", "III", "vol. III"
- Hebrew letters / gematria: "ג", "חלק ג", "ספר ג", "כרך ג", "ה" → 5
- Whole-text mixed: "ספר ג: משפטים" (volume + part title; we only want the number)

## API

```python
def normalize_volume_number(raw: str) -> str:
    """Return a canonical Arabic-digit string for the volume number, or "" if unparseable."""
```

Examples:
- `"v. 3"` → `"3"`
- `"III"` → `"3"`
- `"חלק ג"` → `"3"`
- `"כרך ה: ספר אהבה"` → `"5"`
- `""` or unparseable → `""`

## Implementation notes

- Strip common prefixes ("vol.", "v.", "pt.", "no.", "חלק", "ספר", "כרך", "כתב", "מהדורה") before parsing.
- Try Arabic-digit regex first, then Roman numerals, then gematria.
- Gematria limited to volumes 1..200 is fine (real series dont go higher); table-based mapping rather than full gematria solver.

## Tests

- Pure unit tests in `tests/test_marc_cleanup.py` or a new `tests/test_volume_numbers.py`.
- Cover all four surface forms above, plus edge cases (empty, all-text, leading/trailing whitespace).

title: Per-row override actions and final commit endpoint
description:
Once the matrix has run all its lookups, the user reviews each row, makes overrides, and clicks Commit to finalize. This bead adds the per-row controls and the commit endpoint.

## Per-row endpoints

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/select/?index=N` — change the chosen candidate (when search_status=multiple). Updates `selected_candidate_index`. Returns the row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/skip/` — set `search_status=manual_skip`. Returns the row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/mark-held/` — set `search_status=manual_held` (i.e. user has the volume but no record can be found; will land as a gap-with-`held=True` placeholder).
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/retry/` — reset to `pending`; trigger a fresh lookup (frontend fires the lookup endpoint after re-render).

## Commit endpoint

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/commit/`:
  - `@login_required`, ownership/staff check.
  - Refuse if any row is still `pending` or `searching`.
  - For each row:
    - `found` (or `multiple` with a `selected_candidate_index`): create a Record from the chosen candidate using `_attach_from_candidate`. Update the matching `SeriesVolume(series, volume_number=row.volume_number)` to point at the new Record. Set `row.created_record`.
    - `no_match` or `manual_held`: leave the SeriesVolume placeholder as-is (`record=None, held=True`).
    - `manual_skip`: delete the SeriesVolume for that volume_number (user retracted the claim for this one).
  - Set `claim.status=committed`, `claim.resolved_at=now`.
  - Redirect to the originating Series detail page (or the series_manage view).

## UI

- Each row shows action buttons appropriate to its state (Pick alternate / Skip / Mark held / Retry).
- A single "Commit claim" button at the bottom is disabled while any row is pending or searching.

## Tests

- Unit: each per-row action transitions state correctly and is idempotent.
- Unit: commit creates Records, links SeriesVolumes, sets claim status; refuses while anything pending.
- Unit: skip retracts the SeriesVolume for that number.
- Auth on every endpoint.

## Dependencies

title: Phone-to-desktop handoff for title page scanning
description:
Add a QR-driven phone-to-desktop handoff for the title-page scan ingest path, mirroring the existing barcode/ISBN scan flow. The user opens /ingest/scan-title/ on their laptop, scans a QR code with their phone to authenticate and land on a streamlined capture UI, takes a title-page photo, and reviews the image — from either device — before OCR runs. Confirmation kicks off OCR and proceeds into the existing edit-metadata + cascade-search workflow.

## Goals

- Smooth desktop → phone → camera → desktop loop with one tap each side.
- Image is reviewed (and can be discarded/retaken) before OCR tokens are spent.
- Either device can confirm or discard; the other catches up via polling.
- The existing direct-upload path on desktop stays as an alternative.

## High-level flow

```
Desktop /ingest/scan-title/  ──QR──►  Phone /phone-auth/<token>/
                                           │ sets phone_scan_target=title
                                           ▼
                                      Phone scan-title (streamlined)
                                           │ take photo, upload
                                           ▼
                                  ScanResult.image saved, status=awaiting_ocr
                                           │
                  ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
                  ▼                                                 ▼
         Desktop poll: image card                       Phone shows image card
         [Run OCR] [Discard]                            [Run OCR] [Retake]
                  │
                  ▼
        Either side: Run OCR ──► OCR runs, status=pending,
                                 ocr_output set, edit-metadata UI shown
                                 (existing cascade search continues)

        Either side: Discard ──► image file deleted, status=discarded
                                 (confirmation prompt before delete)
```

## Data model

Extend `ScanResult.STATUS_CHOICES` with a new value `awaiting_ocr` (OCR-only):

| Status         | image | ocr_output | candidate_records | Meaning                                     |
|----------------|-------|------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| awaiting_ocr   | set   | NULL       | []                | (NEW) Image uploaded, OCR not yet run       |
| pending        | set   | set        | populated         | OCR done, awaiting record selection         |
| confirmed      | —     | —          | —                 | Record created                              |
| discarded      | NULL  | —          | —                 | Rejected; image file deleted, row kept      |

Image storage moves from `tmp/title_pages/<uuid>.jpg` to `ScanResult.image` via the existing `ImageField` (already configured for `staging/%Y/%m/%d/`). DB migration required.

## URLs / views

| URL                                      | View                       | Notes |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
| `GET /ingest/qr/?target=title`           | `qr_code_view` (extended)  | Token signs `<user_pk>:<target>`; target ∈ {isbn, title}. |
| `GET /ingest/phone-auth/<token>/`        | `phone_scan_auth` (ext.)   | Sets `phone_scan_target` session key; redirects accordingly. |
| `GET /ingest/scan-title/`                | `title_page_scan` (ext.)   | Renders desktop (QR sidebar + poll pane) or phone (streamlined) variant. |
| `POST /ingest/upload-title/`             | `title_page_upload` (chg.) | Defers OCR. Saves image to `ScanResult.image`, status=awaiting_ocr. Returns phone confirmation in phone mode, image-card partial otherwise. |
| `GET /ingest/scan-title/poll/`           | `title_page_poll` (NEW)    | Returns image cards for the current users awaiting_ocr scans. Polled by desktop and phone. |
| `POST /ingest/scan-title/<id>/ocr/`      | `run_ocr` (NEW)            | Runs OCR on saved image, transitions to pending, returns existing `_ocr_results.html` partial. 409 if already processed. |
| `POST /ingest/scan-title/<id>/discard/`  | `discard_title_scan` (NEW) | Deletes image file (`scan.image.delete(save=False)`), status=discarded. Idempotent. `hx-confirm` on the trigger. |

All write endpoints use `@login_required` and check `scan.scanned_by == request.user or request.user.is_staff`.

## QR token format

Currently signs `str(user_pk)`. Extend to `f"{user_pk}:{target}"`. Backwards compatible: tokens missing the target default to `isbn` so any in-flight QR keeps working.

## UI

**Desktop `/ingest/scan-title/`** (when not phone_scanner):
- Existing direct upload form retained.
- New right sidebar with QR code (mirrors barcode page; `target=title`).
- New "Incoming photos" pane polling `title_page_poll` every 3s.
- Each pending scan: thumbnail + Run OCR / Discard buttons. Discard uses `hx-confirm="Discard this photo?"`.
- Run OCR swaps the card with the existing edit-metadata partial; the cascade-search flow takes over from there unchanged.

**Phone `/ingest/scan-title/`** (when `phone_scan_target=title`):
- Streamlined capture using the existing `<input capture="environment">` UI.
- After upload, replaces form with image card + Run OCR / Retake. Retake calls discard then re-renders capture.
- Lightweight poll on the same endpoint to detect desktop action and avoid stale UI.

## Reuse vs new

- `_scan_poll.html` polling pattern is reused with a new template `_title_page_poll.html` for image cards.
- `_ocr_results.html` partial unchanged — `run_ocr` returns it directly so the cascade-search step is identical to today.
- New `discard_title_scan` rather than overloading existing `discard_scan` (which has ISBN-flow-coupled redirects).

## Error handling & edge cases

- **Upload failure**: phone shows inline error, capture stays available, no partial `ScanResult` created.
- **OCR failure** (`extract_metadata_from_image` returns None): scan stays in `awaiting_ocr`; card shows error with Retry / Discard.
- **Race (both devices act)**: last write wins. `run_ocr` returns 409 if no longer in `awaiting_ocr`. `discard` is idempotent. Both polls reconcile.
- **Token expiry / wrong target**: `TimestampSigner` already validates max_age=3600. Missing target → isbn (back-compat). Unknown target → 400.
- **Image cleanup**: `scan.image.delete(save=False)` on disk; `image=None`, `status=discarded` in DB; row kept for audit.
- **Stale awaiting_ocr rows**: out of scope for v1; consider a janitor command later.
- **Phone session conflict**: `phone_scan_target` overwritten on each `phone-auth` hit.

## Testing

Per CLAUDE.md, user-visible workflow changes require Playwright e2e coverage.

**Unit tests** (`ingest/tests.py`):
- QR token round-trip (valid, expired, malformed, missing target → isbn default).
- Deferred-upload: status=awaiting_ocr, image saved, OCR not invoked.
- `run_ocr`: happy path, 409 on already-processed, OCR-None error, auth check.
- `discard_title_scan`: file deleted, status set, idempotent, auth check.
- `title_page_poll`: returns only requesting users awaiting_ocr scans.

**E2e tests** (`tests/e2e/`):
- Two browser contexts (desktop + phone); phone navigates a generated `phone-auth` URL.
- Phone uploads fixture title-page image → desktop poll → desktop Run OCR (Claude Vision patched at boundary, since `pytest-socket` blocks live HTTP) → metadata edit → cascade search (also patched) → record created.
- Phone uploads → desktop discards (with confirm) → image gone, status=discarded, phone poll reverts to capture.

Fixture: small JPG under `tests/fixtures/title_pages/`, no real bibliographic content.

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- Multi-page (title + verso) capture and merged OCR.
- Janitor command to prune stale awaiting_ocr rows.
- In-browser rotation / cropping before OCR.
- Phone landing screen offering both barcode and title-page capture from one QR.

## Child beads

This epic is implemented through these child beads (created with this epic):
1. Extend QR/auth flow to support per-target scan landing.
2. Add awaiting_ocr status + use ScanResult.image for title-page uploads.
3. Defer OCR in title_page_upload; add run_ocr endpoint.
4. Add title_page_poll view and image-card partial.
5. Update scan-title template: desktop QR sidebar + poll pane; phone streamlined view.
6. Add discard_title_scan endpoint with image cleanup + confirmation.
7. E2e Playwright test for full handoff flow.

title: Series-aware ingest with auto-fetch and matrix review
description:
When a scanned volume is part of a multi-volume series, let the user claim the whole set (or any subset) in one action. The system auto-fetches sibling volumes from the source catalogs, presents a live-updating matrix the user can review and override row-by-row, then commits the accepted records and links them to a single Series with appropriate SeriesVolume entries.

Builds on existing infrastructure: `Series`, `SeriesVolume(record nullable, held bool)`, `series_workflow.create_series_volumes` (already parses "1-5" / "all 5" / "1-2, 4-7, 10").

Originally raised in feedback from @shalomhav on issue #4 (https://github.com/dchud/otzar/issues/4) and refined in conversation about volume-3-of-5 cases where one record carries the volume designation but the total is only known to the user.

## User flow

1. User scans an ISBN; queue surfaces candidates from NLI/LC/etc as today.
2. A candidate with series info shows a new "Claim series" affordance alongside "Use this record".
3. Click opens a small form: "Volumes you have" (text input parsed as range/list/all-N).
4. Submit:
   - Match or create the `Series` (by title + author normalization).
   - Create a `Record` for the originally-scanned volume from the chosen candidate.
   - Create `SeriesVolume` placeholders (`held=True, record=None`) for all other volume numbers in the spec.
   - Persist a `SeriesClaim` row tracking which volumes are still being searched.
5. Redirect to the matrix view. Each row triggers its own HTMX-driven catalog search on load (parallel browser-driven fan-out — no background workers needed).
6. Each row updates live: pending → searching → "found candidate(s)" / "no match" / "multiple — pick one".
7. User reviews and edits per-row (skip, choose alternate candidate, mark as gap-only).
8. Single "Commit" button creates Records for accepted candidates, links them to their SeriesVolumes, and resolves the claim.

## Honest caveats baked into the UX

- Each auto-fetch is best-effort: search by series title + filter by 490$v/830$v will sometimes return wrong/ambiguous results. The matrix shows the candidate so the user can veto.
- Volume numbers come in Arabic digits, Hebrew letters/gematria, Roman numerals — fuzzy matching needed (own bead).
- Some volumes wont be in any catalog. Those stay as `held=True, record=None` placeholders.
- Rate limits: cascade fires N searches in fast succession; existing cascade tolerates this but worth monitoring.

## Data model additions

- New `SeriesClaim` model — transient (or kept-for-audit) tracking of an in-progress claim:
  - `series` (FK, nullable until matched)
  - `created_by`, `created_at`, `resolved_at`
  - `volume_spec` (raw user input string)
  - `originating_scan` (FK to ScanResult)
  - `originating_volume_number` (string)
  - `status` (pending / committed / cancelled)
- New `SeriesClaimRow` (one per volume in the spec):
  - `claim` (FK)
  - `volume_number` (string)
  - `search_status` (pending / searching / found / no_match / multiple / manual_skip / manual_held)
  - `candidate_records` (JSONField — same shape as `ScanResult.candidate_records`)
  - `selected_candidate_index` (nullable int)
  - `created_record` (nullable FK)

This keeps the persistent `Series`/`SeriesVolume` model clean: claims and their per-volume search state live separately and can be discarded after commit.

## Architecture / endpoints (sketch — child beads refine)

- `POST /ingest/scan/<scan_id>/claim-series/` — create the SeriesClaim and SeriesVolume placeholders; redirect to matrix.
- `GET /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/` — render the matrix.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/lookup/` — run the catalog search for one row; HTMX fires this on row load. Returns the updated row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/select/` — user picks an alternate candidate or marks skip/held.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/commit/` — finalize.

## Volume number matching

Need a `normalize_volume_number(s) -> str` helper that maps Hebrew letters and gematria, Roman numerals, and Arabic digits to a canonical form for comparison. (See bd children for details.)

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- @shalomhavs "keep scanning more volumes from the same series" UX — auto-detect on subsequent ISBN scans that we already have a Series for this title, offer to attach. Distinct ergonomics from the claim-the-set workflow; lower priority once auto-fetch ships.
- Rate-limit-aware sequential search (current model is browser-driven fan-out, parallel).
- Series authority enrichment (look up 800/810/811 series authority records to disambiguate series with similar titles).

## Child beads

1. Surface volume part metadata (245$n / 245$p) in MARC parser, candidates, queue.
2. Persist Series + SeriesVolume on single-scan confirm.
3. Volume number normalization helper (Hebrew / gematria / Roman / Arabic).
4. Per-volume catalog lookup helper.
5. Data model: SeriesClaim + SeriesClaimRow + migration.
6. Claim form on queue card + create-claim endpoint + initial matrix render.
7. Per-row HTMX lookup endpoint + live matrix updates.
8. Per-row override actions + final commit endpoint.
9. E2e Playwright test for the full claim flow with patched cascades.

title: Per-volume catalog lookup helper
description:
Add a helper that, given a series identifier and a target volume number, queries the source-catalog cascade and returns ranked candidates whose volume number matches.

## API

```python
def find_series_volume(
    series_title: str,
    author: str | None,
    volume_number: str,
) -> list[dict]:
    """Search NLI/LC for a specific volume of a known series.

    Returns a list of candidate records (same shape as
    `sources.cascade.search_*`), filtered to those whose 490\$v / 830\$v
    normalize to the requested volume_number. Empty list = no match.
    """
```

## Implementation

- Compose a search query targeting the catalogs title index, scoped to series titles when supported. Fall back to a generic title search.
- For each cascade-returned candidate, compute `normalize_volume_number(candidate.series_volume)` (using the sibling bead bd-ra1 helper) and keep those that equal the normalized target.
- Sort matches by (a) series title similarity, (b) author match, (c) source catalog preference (NLI first for Hebrew titles, LC otherwise — matches existing cascade order).

## Tests

- Unit: mocked cascade returns three candidates with different volume numbers; helper returns only the one matching the requested volume.
- Unit: candidate without series_volume is filtered out.
- Unit: no candidates returned when none match.
- Edge: helper does NOT raise on cascade exceptions (logs and returns []).

## Dependencies

- bd-ra1 (volume number normalization).

Bead: bd-zwg (parent epic)

title: Configure Django for production behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy
description:
The container runs behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS (Caddy on the instance, per bd-n7a). Django sees plain HTTP from the proxy, so in production `request.is_secure()` is False, the session and CSRF cookies are sent without the Secure flag, and `manage.py check --deploy` reports W004 (HSTS), W012 (`SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`) and W016 (`CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE`). The QR handoff in `ingest/views.py` works around the scheme problem by inferring https from `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`; once the proxy header is trusted that inference is unnecessary but harmless.

A second gap: Django's default logging sends the `django` logger to the console only while `DEBUG` is true and routes request errors to `mail_admins`, which is not configured. A 500 in production therefore leaves nothing but gunicorn's access-log line.

## Changes

All in `otzar/settings.py`, keyed on `DEBUG` being false so local development is unchanged:

- `SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER = ("HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO", "https")`. This is safe only when every request reaches gunicorn through the proxy. In the deployment gunicorn listens on the Docker network and only Caddy can reach it; say so in a comment next to the setting, because the setting is a vulnerability on any host where gunicorn is reachable directly.
- `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True`, `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True`.
- `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS`: pick a value and record the choice. A short one (an hour) is safe to start with and can be raised once the site has served https for a while; or leave HSTS to Caddy, which does not set it by default. Either is fine; the point is a deliberate decision rather than the warning.
- Leave `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` off. Caddy redirects http to https itself; W008 stays and is expected.
- `LOGGING`: a console handler at INFO for `django`, `django.request` and the project apps, active regardless of `DEBUG`, so tracebacks reach the container's stdout where `docker compose logs` collects them.
- `entrypoint.sh`: gunicorn's `--forwarded-allow-ips` defaults to `127.0.0.1`, which is the proxy's address only when both run in the same network namespace. With Caddy on the host and gunicorn in a container the request arrives from the Docker bridge address, and gunicorn strips the forwarded headers before Django sees them. Read the value from an environment variable (`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`) that the deployment sets.

## Tests

Unit tests: with `DEBUG=false` the settings resolve as above; a request carrying `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is `is_secure()`; the QR handoff URL built from such a request starts with `https://`. E2e: N/A, nothing a user sees changes on local storage.

## Platform

None. This applies on any host where a proxy fronts the container. It has to land before the first deploy.

title: Store media in S3 through a storage backend selected by environment
description:
`MEDIA_ROOT` is `DATA_DIR/media`, and `otzar/urls.py` mounts `/media/` only when `DEBUG` is true. A production deployment today serves no images at all: `ScanResult.image.url` and `TitlePageImage.image.url` render to `/media/...` paths that nothing answers. Something has to serve media before the first deploy. bd-n7a recommends S3 through Django's storage API rather than the instance disk; the reasoning and the alternative are recorded there.

What the code already does right: every access goes through the storage API. OCR reads the photo with `scan.image.open("rb")`, discard removes it with `scan.image.delete()`, templates use `.url`; nothing reads `.path`. So this is a dependency and a settings switch, not application code.

## Changes

- Add `django-storages[s3]` (which brings `boto3`) to the dependencies.
- In `otzar/settings.py`, when `AWS_S3_MEDIA_BUCKET` is set, configure `STORAGES["default"]` as `storages.backends.s3.S3Storage` with the bucket and region, `file_overwrite` off, a private default ACL, and query-string authentication on, so `.url` yields a presigned URL (default expiry 3600 s) and objects are reachable only through URLs the app hands out. When the variable is unset, keep `FileSystemStorage`: local development, CI and both test suites do not change.
- Credentials: `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` from the environment, which boto3 reads on its own; on a host with an instance role they can be omitted. `.env.example` and the configuration table in `docs/administration.md` say no code reads the `AWS_*` variables; after this ticket the media bucket variable is read, and the backup bucket variables are read by the Litestream ticket. Rewrite both to describe what each variable does.
- Keep the upload paths as they are (`staging/YYYY/MM/DD/<uuid>.jpg`, `title-pages/YYYY/MM/DD/`). The backend adds no prefix. The provisioning ticket turns on versioning and a 30-day noncurrent-version expiry on the bucket; that is the media backup.
- `cleanup_staging` (bd-4jn) walks a directory with `os.listdir`. Whoever rewrites it must go through `default_storage.listdir` and `delete` so it works on both backends; note that on bd-4jn.
- bd-yg9 moves a file from staging to its permanent path. Through the storage API a move is read, save, delete; on S3 that is a copy and a delete. No special handling.

## Tests

Unit tests for the settings switch (variable set and unset) and for the storage class and URL shape. The S3 code path is not exercised by CI. If a round-trip test (save, open, delete) with `moto` stays under a few dozen lines, add it; otherwise the deploy ticket's smoke test covers it: upload a title-page photo on the deployed site and confirm the image renders. E2e: N/A, no user-visible change on local storage.

## Alternative

Media on the instance disk: no Python change; Caddy serves `/media/*` with `file_server` rooted at `DATA_DIR/media`; a timer runs `aws s3 sync` hourly into the versioned bucket; the restore drill gains a sync-back step; the instance disk becomes a second system of record. If the owner prefers this, this ticket becomes a Caddy block and a timer in the provisioning ticket, and the storage-API discipline still holds.

## Platform

None. Only the bucket is AWS, and any S3-compatible endpoint works through `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL`.

title: Replicate the database to S3 with Litestream and take daily snapshots
description:
Two mechanisms, as bd-n7a lays out: continuous replication, which covers losing the machine, and dated snapshots, which cover a mistake noticed later. Both live in the container image, so they work on any Docker host with a local disk. Nothing here is Lightsail-specific.

## Litestream

- Install the Litestream release binary in the image and pin the version. 0.5.x replaced the WAL-segment format with LTX; the keys below are 0.5 semantics, so check the reference for the pinned version.
- Configuration at `/etc/litestream.yml`, written by the entrypoint from the environment: one database, `${DATA_DIR}/db.sqlite3`; one replica, `s3://${AWS_S3_BACKUP_BUCKET}/litestream/db` in `${AWS_S3_REGION}`. Credentials come from the standard `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` variables, which Litestream reads itself and which fall back to an instance role on a host that has one.
- Settings: `sync-interval` at its 1 s default; `snapshot.interval: 24h`; `snapshot.retention: 168h`, so any moment in the last seven days is restorable with `-timestamp`. The default retention is 24 h, which is too short to be useful for a mistake noticed the next day. Leave `l0-retention` at its default.
- Entrypoint order. First, refuse to start when `DATA_DIR` is unset or resolves to `/app`: an unset `DATA_DIR` runs against the image's own filesystem, and the next redeploy discards the catalog. The Dockerfile's `DATABASE_URL` line is dead (settings read `DATA_DIR`) and can go at the same time. Second, `litestream restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists -o "$DATA_DIR/db.sqlite3" <replica>`, so a fresh disk pulls the latest copy before migrate runs. Third, `litestream replicate -exec "<migrate, then gunicorn>"`, so replication is running while migrations write. Litestream exits when the child exits.
- An environment switch (`LITESTREAM_DISABLED=1` or an empty bucket variable) that skips both Litestream steps and runs the child directly. The restore drill needs it: a drill instance that runs the production entrypoint would replicate into the production replica path.
- Local check before merging: run the image against a scratch bucket (or MinIO through the `endpoint` field), create a record, and confirm LTX objects appear under the replica path.

## Daily snapshot

- A management command (`snapshot_db` or similar) that copies the live database with `sqlite3.Connection.backup()`, the online-backup API, which is safe against a WAL database in use, to a temporary file under `DATA_DIR`; gzips it; uploads it with boto3 to `s3://<backup bucket>/snapshots/YYYY/MM/DD/db.sqlite3.gz`; and writes `manifest.json` beside it holding the record count, the commit from `settings.BUILD_INFO`, and the timestamp. On the first of the month it also copies the pair to `monthly/YYYY/MM/`. It writes `snapshots/latest.json` (same content) so backup freshness is one GET.
- Scheduling is the host's job: a systemd timer (or cron) runs `docker compose exec app python manage.py snapshot_db` daily. The provisioning ticket installs the timer. The deploy script runs the same command before pulling a new image; that snapshot is the rollback point for a bad migration.
- Lifecycle rules on the bucket, set by the provisioning ticket: `snapshots/` expires after 35 days, `monthly/` after 400 days, `litestream/` is left to Litestream's own retention. At this catalog's size the storage is cents a month.
- Not backed up, on purpose: `DATA_DIR/cache` (derived from the database) and `staticfiles` (built into the image).

## Docs and tests

The backup section of `docs/administration.md` describes the two mechanisms, what each protects against, and the retention windows. The restore procedure moves to the write-up the restore drill ticket produces. A unit test runs the snapshot command against local storage with the S3 client stubbed and checks the manifest. The Litestream path is verified by the restore drill, not by a unit test.

title: Provision the Lightsail instance, S3 buckets and IAM user with a script
description:
The platform-specific ticket. bd-n7a recommends Lightsail; if the owner chooses EC2 instead, this is the ticket that changes (instance creation, an instance role instead of an IAM user, EBS snapshots through Data Lifecycle Manager instead of Lightsail's automatic snapshots), and the other tickets in the set stay as they are.

## Deliverable

`scripts/provision.sh`, driven by the AWS CLI with one region variable, idempotent where the API allows, plus the provisioning section of `docs/deployment.md`. A shell script rather than Terraform: one instance, two buckets and one user do not justify a state file to store and a second tool to learn, and the script is the record of what exists. The script stops where an operator has to type a secret.

## Instance

- Lightsail, the 1 GB / 2 vCPU / 40 GB dual-stack Linux bundle ($7 a month), Ubuntu 24.04 LTS blueprint, in the region nearest the users. The root disk persists across stop and start and is what snapshots capture; a separate block-storage disk is not needed at this size.
- A static IP attached to the instance. Firewall: 22 (key-only SSH), 80, 443.
- Automatic snapshots on: daily, seven kept, about $0.05 per GB-month of snapshot data. These roll back the machine (OS, Docker, Caddy, `.env`), not the catalog; the catalog's backups are in S3.
- A launch script (user data) that installs Docker with the Compose plugin, Caddy, and the AWS CLI; creates a 1 GB swap file; creates `/opt/otzar` with `compose.yml`, `Caddyfile`, `deploy.sh` and the snapshot timer unit (all kept in the repo under `deploy/`), and `/opt/otzar/data` as `DATA_DIR`.
- `compose.yml`: one service, the GHCR image, `DATA_DIR` bind-mounted, port 8000 published on 127.0.0.1 only. `Caddyfile`: the site hostname, `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000`. Caddy obtains the certificate from Let's Encrypt and redirects http to https.
- DNS: an A record for the hostname to the static IP. If DNS stays at the registrar there is no Route 53 cost.
- Upgrade path, for the docs: Lightsail cannot resize in place. Snapshot, launch the 2 GB bundle from the snapshot, move the static IP. About fifteen minutes of downtime.

## S3

Two buckets in the instance's region, both with public access blocked and versioning on: a media bucket (served by the app through presigned URLs) and a backup bucket (never served). Lifecycle: media noncurrent versions expire after 30 days; on the backup bucket, `snapshots/` after 35 days and `monthly/` after 400 days, with `litestream/` left alone. Two buckets rather than prefixes because the media bucket is reachable through the app and the backup bucket must never be.

## IAM

Lightsail instances cannot assume an instance role, so the box holds a static access key. One IAM user (`otzar-instance`) with one inline policy allowing `s3:ListBucket`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject` and `s3:DeleteObject` on exactly the two buckets (Litestream deletes expired files, so `DeleteObject` is required). One access key, written into `/opt/otzar/.env` (root, mode 0600) and nowhere else. Document rotation: create a second key, replace it in `.env`, restart, delete the first. A second, read-only user for the restore drill, created by the drill ticket.

## Secrets

`/opt/otzar/.env` holds `SECRET_KEY`, `DEBUG=false`, `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, `DATA_DIR`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_MODEL`, `SITE_PASSWORD`, `RECORD_ID_PREFIX`, `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`, the two bucket names, the region and the access key. It is written by hand from `.env.example` during provisioning; the script prints the template and waits. GitHub never holds application secrets. A Lightsail snapshot includes the file, which is acceptable inside one account.

## Deploy access

An SSH keypair used only by the deploy workflow: the public key in the instance's `authorized_keys`, the private key as the `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` repository secret, the host as the `DEPLOY_HOST` repository variable.

## First start and verification

`docker compose up -d` once by hand; `createsuperuser` through `docker compose exec`. Then: `https://<hostname>/health/` returns 200 from outside; the certificate is valid; after creating one record, LTX objects appear under `litestream/` in the backup bucket. Record the instance name, static IP, bucket names and region in `docs/deployment.md`.

## Cost

About $7 a month for the instance, under $1 for snapshots and S3 combined. bd-n7a has the comparison with EC2.

title: Deploy on push to main by building the image and restarting the container over SSH
description:
One push. Merging to `main` builds the image, pushes it, and restarts the container on the instance. `just deploy` runs the last step by hand for emergencies and for the restore drill.

## Workflow

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, triggered by `workflow_run` on the CI workflow completing successfully on `main`, so a deploy never runs on a red main. Steps: check out the commit CI tested; build the image for `linux/amd64` (add `linux/arm64` on an `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner only if the host is Graviton); tag `ghcr.io/dchud/otzar:<sha>` and `:latest`; push with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the repository is public, so the package is public and costs nothing); SSH to `DEPLOY_HOST` with `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` and run `/opt/otzar/deploy.sh <sha>`.

## deploy.sh

Kept in the repo under `deploy/` and copied to the host by provisioning. In order: run `docker compose exec app python manage.py snapshot_db`, the pre-deploy snapshot and the rollback point; set the image tag compose reads; `docker compose pull` and `docker compose up -d`, after which the entrypoint finds the database in place, migrates, and starts gunicorn; poll `https://<host>/health/` for up to 60 s; print the age of the newest object under `litestream/` and of `snapshots/latest.json`. Any failure exits non-zero and fails the workflow.

Migrations run automatically, as `entrypoint.sh` does today. Rollback is the restore procedure applied to the pre-deploy snapshot, then `just deploy <previous sha>`; previous tags stay in GHCR. Migrations are reviewed for being non-destructive before merge, as now.

## Manual path

`just deploy [sha]` runs the same SSH command from a laptop that holds the key; `just deploy-logs` tails `docker compose logs`; `just backup-status` prints the two ages above. The recipes take the host from `DEPLOY_HOST` in the local environment.

## Secrets

GitHub holds the deploy key and the host, nothing else. Application secrets stay in the instance's `.env` and the workflow never reads them.

## Smoke test

After the first deploy, and whenever this pipeline changes: log in, scan a title page from a phone through the QR handoff, confirm the image renders (this is the S3 media path, which CI does not exercise), confirm a search returns the new record.

## Docs

`docs/deployment.md` is empty. Write it: where the instance and buckets are (pointer to the provisioning script), how a deploy happens, how to roll back, where secrets live and how to rotate them, how to read logs. Update "Applying code updates" in `docs/administration.md` to point at the deploy rather than a `git pull`.

## Rejected alternative

A poller on the host (Watchtower or similar) pulling `latest` needs no inbound SSH but loses the pre-deploy snapshot and the health gate, and gives no signal in the pull request when a deploy fails.

## Platform

The SSH target is any Docker host with the compose files in place; only the address is Lightsail's.

## Tests

The first deploy exercises the workflow. Run `shellcheck` over `deploy.sh` in `scripts/check.sh` if it is cheap to add. E2e: N/A.

title: Run a restore from S3 onto a throwaway instance and record the result
description:
The deliverable bd-n7a names: a restore that has been executed and verified, not described. Until this has been run once, the backups are unverified.

## Guard

The drill instance must not touch production data. Give it a read-only IAM user (`s3:ListBucket`, `s3:GetObject` on both buckets) and set the entrypoint's replication switch off, so it cannot write into the production replica path or the media bucket. Uploads on the drill instance fail; that is expected. Do not attach the production hostname.

## Procedure

Script what can be scripted as `scripts/restore-drill.sh`; the rest goes in `docs/administration.md`.

1. Before restoring, read from production: `Record.objects.count()`, and for one record chosen at drill time its id, title, authors and identifiers. These are the values to compare against.
2. Launch a throwaway instance with the provisioning script (Lightsail: a second 1 GB instance, billed by the hour, deleted at the end) with the read-only key and replication disabled.
3. Restore path A, Litestream: `litestream restore -o "$DATA_DIR/db.sqlite3" s3://<backup bucket>/litestream/db` for the latest state; then once more with `-timestamp` set to an hour earlier, to prove point-in-time restore works. Restore path B, snapshot: download `snapshots/<date>/db.sqlite3.gz`, gunzip into place, remove any `-wal` and `-shm` files beside it. Run both paths; each is a fresh container start.
4. Start the container. The entrypoint migrates, which is a no-op when the image matches production.
5. Verify, recording each value:
   - Record count equals the manifest's count (path B) or production's count at step 1 (path A), allowing for records created in between and saying how many.
   - The chosen record's title, authors and identifiers match step 1.
   - `search_records("<a word from that title>")` returns that record. The FTS table and its shadow tables are in the same file, so both paths should carry the index. If the search returns nothing while the count is right, run `manage.py reindex`, search again, and record that a rebuild was needed.
   - The chosen record's image, or a `ScanResult.image`, returns 200 through the drill instance's pages. With media on S3 this needs no restore step; if the owner chose disk media, `aws s3 sync` it back first and verify.
   - `/health/` returns 200 through Caddy.
   - Backup freshness on production: the newest `litestream/` object is younger than an hour after a write, and `snapshots/latest.json` is younger than 25 hours.
6. Delete the throwaway instance.
7. Record in `docs/administration.md`: date, image commit, which snapshot and which timestamp, the counts, the record id checked, whether a reindex was needed, and elapsed time. Keep the last three entries.

## Repeating it

Repeat after any change to the entrypoint, the Litestream configuration or the snapshot command, and otherwise about quarterly. Nothing automates the reminder; the write-up should say so and the owner puts it on a calendar.

## Platform

Launching the throwaway instance is the only Lightsail-specific step. Tests: the drill is the test; unit and e2e are N/A.
